messages:
alice_support: Heads-up: ACME is seeing an uptick of 502s hitting the hosted API since ~15:03 UTC in eu-west. Roughly 18% of in-flight requests for tenant acme-123 are returning 502 from the edge. Sample trace id: trace=trc_9f2a. curl to frontdoor returns 502 consistently for long-poll calls.

raj_oncall: looking now. any recent deploys to frontdoor / splitter?

alice_support: No deployments flagged by deploy-bot. deploy-bot: no deploys in last 6h. Logs show a lot of upstream reset/connection errors in envoy:
```
[2024-09-04T15:03:14Z] envoy upstream reset: connection failure, stream error
[2024-09-04T15:03:14Z] envoy rls: cluster "splitter-eu1" returned reset for request id=trc_9f2a
```

lena_eng_sre: Can you paste the raw request headers (redact tokens) and a short curl sample? curious about a big header or tenant metadata that could be triggering fanout.

alice_support: curl sample: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Tenant: acme-123" -d @payload.json https://frontdoor.eu-west.redwood.ai/v1/generate` Payload is long-lived SSE stream. Headers: `X-Tenant-Meta: v=2024;features=embeds,stream;context=lots-of-metadata` — the tenant metadata is a 6kB header blob.

lena_eng_sre: aha — header size that big + streaming can cause the splitter to create multiple upstream connections and exhaust h2 stream/window. This can surface as upstream resets and 502s. Not a code deploy. Could be queue/backpressure behavior in splitter when many tenants have large metadata.

marta_prod: Is this only ACME or other tenants? Metrics show a small cluster of tenants with similar header sizes but only acme is in the red right now. They have a big batch of concurrent streams.

raj_oncall: Mitigation options: 1) short-term throttle per-tenant (reduce concurrency) 2) enable fallback routing to secondary pool that has looser keepalive settings 3) ask ACME to trim metadata on client side. I can flip a per-tenant concurrency cap for acme-123 now.

alice_support: Please do 1) and 2) if possible. Customer is hitting prod traffic. I pinged acme_ops to ask them to reduce metadata size. @acme_ops any chance you can trim or move metadata to body?

acme_ops: We're on it — will try trimming the X-Tenant-Meta and test. ETA ~20m. We also can batch less frequently.

raj_oncall: Done: applied temporary concurrency cap 8 -> 2 for tenant acme-123 on splitter-eu1. Also flipped routing: acme now hitting backup-splitter-eu1 with increased h2 window config. Monitoring now.

lena_eng_sre: I'm watching envoy metrics and connection resets dropped ~90% after the cap + reroute. Trace trc_9f2a now returns 200 for repeated curl attempts. Looks like backpressure caused splitter to drop upstreams.

marta_prod: Logging note: capture envoy config for the affected splitter and upload to the incident bucket: `s3://redwood-support/incidents/1713509876/`. Also add tenant id to the alerting rule for future bursts.

alice_support: Customer confirmed reduced errors after we trimmed headers and applied cap. They saw successful streaming resumes. :thumbsup:

tim_devex: Let's add a short doc in docs/quickstarts about header size guidance for streaming tenants — observed issues with >4k header blob + heavy concurrency. I'll drop a PR.

lena_eng_sre: Followups: 1) run a load test with large X-Tenant-Meta header against splitter to tune defaults. 2) consider default per-tenant concurrency cap in splitter to avoid noisy-tenant effects. 3) add an alert when a single tenant consumes >20% of splitter streams.

raj_oncall: I'll add alert and schedule load test with qa infra. Thanks everyone. Closing thread when PRs + alert are linked here.

alice_support: Filing post-incident notes and customer comms. Will update support ticket.

marta_prod: PR for alert and runbook: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/merge/1234 (draft). Load test task: infra-2456.

alice_support: last check 15:45 UTC we see normal rates. Closing for now.
